correctness.rationale: Compact support inside the positive quadrant makes the logarithmic generator tests regular. If either variance vanishes, invariant-support tangency forces the unique positive equilibrium. The packaged checker independently verifies all algebraic reductions.

value.rationale: The Lotka–Volterra predator–prey cycle is a canonical example in which the two populations are visibly phase-coupled and constrained to a nonlinear closed orbit. The theorem shows that this strong nonlinear dependence is invisible to every one-coordinate linear regression: each conditional mean is exactly flat and the full-period Pearson correlation is exactly zero at every orbit amplitude. That is a structurally stronger and practically different statement from the familiar equality of time averages with equilibrium values. The variance identities further identify each population's fluctuation energy exactly with the mean square per-capita growth rate of the other species, giving parameter-exact consistency checks for periodic-orbit data and simulations.
